# Reducing Stress

[Stress](psychoed_stressful_event.html) is one of the most common pathways to relapse. While alcohol may provide short-term relief, it typically worsens stress over time by disrupting sleep, increasing conflict in relationships, and reducing the ability to think clearly and solve problems.

Sustained recovery improves when stress is noticed early and addressed directly, rather than avoided or numbed. A practical framework is: **Reduce avoidable stress, tolerate unavoidable stress, and recover daily.**

-   Reduce avoidable stress by changing what you can (boundaries, time use, workload, environment)
-   Tolerate unavoidable stress by building skills to stay grounded without reacting impulsively
-   Recover daily by intentionally resetting your mind and body, even in small ways

Stress reduction alone is not enough. Daily recovery is essential. Brief, consistent recovery practices help regulate the nervous system, improve self-control, and reduce vulnerability to high-risk decisions.

![](https://github.com/jjcurtin/aud_support/blob/main/modules/images/stressreduction.jpeg?raw=true){fig-align="center"}

::: callout-important
### Practice Plan

-   Apply this in real situations, not just on paper.
-   Choose one stressor you can change and take a small, specific action
-   Choose one stressor you cannot change and practice a coping skill
-   Keep the steps simple and repeatable

**If something feels overwhelming, scale it down rather than avoiding it. Consistency matters more than intensity.**
:::
